decision: Keep all four policies experimental. Early release saves acquisition time versus 2 MiB retention but has mixed signs against original 4 MiB retention. Cleanup alone does not improve solve mean. The pending cap changes scope; neither the full-visit envelope nor the target allocation trace demonstrates a substantial memory saving. Proof storage and structural coverage are unchanged.
limitations: Previous 114/138 holdout is exposed. Fresh 120/144, seed 202611240203: 72 queries, 48 distinct roots, six families. Freeze before fresh evaluation; no outcome filtering.

Four alternating serial repetitions compare full-visit retention at 2 MiB; reference cleanup with the same full-visit charging; cleanup plus early budget transfer at 2 MiB; and original retention at 4 MiB. The larger control is motivated by the 3.92 MB full-visit envelope on exposed case 37, not by fresh outcomes.
Every arm starts empty with native cap 256 and unchanged pool/discovery priority. Only source CNFs enter search. Novelty against all six parent tables supplies no answers.

Mutable private leases are cleared when canonicalization and any needed propagation finish. Unvisited offers and unconsumed propagation remain charged. All proof checking suppresses hints; checked prefixes survive stops.

Early release changes the charge scope: pending preparation is bounded, but native visits still own their required data. Record a separate conservative full-visit envelope that keeps each released charge until its visit returns. It can exceed 2 MiB. This is not a whole-process memory bound or proof of lower RAM.

Lease headers include an extra state slot charged by the same conservative estimator. Control containers, frames, allocator overhead and construction transients are outside that cap. Selected retained solver graph and RSS are measured separately.

Charge sizing, freezing, failed admission, matching, copies, disposal, recognition, checking, persistence, serialization, warm/cold replay/reconstruction and compression. Worker timers exclude imports, source hashing, case loading and final report bookkeeping.
Two exposed 38-query exact-prefix diagnostics compare early release and the 4 MiB retention control. Their timing and cumulative preservation/profile work are outside matched means.

No new table, proof authority, persistent hint or production default. Exclusive synchronous execution only. Identical native search and certificate bytes are required, not inferred from aggregate coverage.
Every preceding authority payload is unchanged; raw archives preserve alternative proofs. All six table payloads are byte-identical across the four arms of each matched stream.
Two readers verify all retained nodes, including budget-stopped prefixes, and all 342 prior partitions. Per-query ID logs track four authority tables; independent replay checks all six.
No nonconflicting propagation or local preparation offer confers verdict authority. Exact correspondence tests and unchanged proof checkers are separate obligations.

Early release bounds pending preparation, not native visit data. The separate full-visit envelope retains all transferred charges until their visits end and can exceed the nominal cap. Clearing references does not imply that the native computation no longer needs those objects.

The mutable-lease control retains full-visit charges. It includes carrier/header and accounting changes; comparing that control with early release isolates the release policy. Original 4 MiB retention prices simply increasing capacity.
Cumulative validation, compression, diagnostics and profiling are outside matched means; transport chunking does not reduce logical storage growth.
Posthoc selection chooses the largest mean unresolved early-release attempt among four fresh repetitions; this is not a new holdout or an algorithmic gate.
Each exact chronological prefix starts empty and matches status/counters. Every retained payload equals one already archived in its matched worker.
Profiler overhead is outside comparative means; cumulative function times overlap. Structure labels are diagnostic only.

A separate exact-prefix replay starts tracemalloc after garbage collection immediately before the target attempt. Its peak includes new Python allocations and attempt bookkeeping, excludes existing prefix state and native memory, and is not a whole-process RAM bound. Results and all retained payloads match the untraced worker.
All 64 earlier proof environments are unchanged. The full suite retains pre-existing SQLite ResourceWarnings.
Timing signs and regressions remain visible across all four pairs. No population speedup or process-memory bound is inferred from selected payload accounting.
Old authoritative payloads and failed development checks remain preserved; the cumulative union can grow even when each policy produces identical current-stream proofs.
